items.note: Self-ID has risen since 2022 and estimates range ~0.5-1.6%. Cite the year.

items.ask: Out of every 100 Americans, how many are Christian?

Out of every 100 American adults, how many are married?
items.note: Nearly right. Groups near 50% are estimated well. This is the item that proves the pattern is compression toward the middle rather than general innumeracy.

queued.note: Real leads, numbers NOT yet verified. Do not publish any of these until the primary source is read.
mines: Ipsos 'Perils of Perception' — runs annually across ~30 countries since 2014. Dozens of items per wave on immigration, obesity, teen pregnancy, murder rate, vaccination, wealth distribution. Probably the single richest source of remaining items.

Gapminder / Factfulness 13-question test — global poverty, girls' schooling, life expectancy, vaccination, natural disasters. 2017, ~12,000 respondents in 14 countries, average score 2 of 12, and about 80% did worse than random. The 'chimpanzee benchmark' is here.

Gallup crime series — majorities say crime rose in almost every year including long stretches when it fell. ~80% said crime rose in 2023, when it fell. Violent victimisation went 80 per 1,000 (1994) to 19 per 1,000 (2010).
Bobby Duffy, 'The Perils of Perception' (2018) — book-length compilation of the Ipsos waves, good index of items.
Ahler & Sood follow-ups and the MTurk replications in the same paper (n = 382 / 1,036 / 821) — gives per-party breakdowns of the same eight items.
More in Common 2021-22 'history wars' application of the same method.
Causes-of-death misperception (Our World in Data has the media-coverage-vs-actual-deaths comparison: terrorism and homicide massively over-covered, heart disease and cancer under-covered).
Ingroup-norm misperception, PNAS Nexus 2024 — people also overestimate how much their OWN side dislikes the other. This is the 'undercounting your own side' direction and it is the one nobody builds.
